name: Pale Turtle Green
lede: Pale Turtle Green is a dusty yellow-green named, like its darker sibling Turtle Green, for the color of a tortoise or turtle's shell rather than any plant.

sections.title: A shell color, not a plant one
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 color standards place this swatch on plate XXXII, hue 31, tone f [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system, citing the same plate, classes it in block 119 [1]. The name groups it with the handful of Ridgway shell colors rather than with the many plant greens, which is why ColorHub's tagging keeps it under nature rather than a dye or pigment [1]. Its darker sibling, plain Turtle Green, sits closer to an actual shell's olive back; this pale version reads closer to a dry, sun-bleached straw [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[seafoam]], [[lemon-meringue]] and [[amber-white]], at 3.4, [[khaki]] and [[cream]] sit in the same muted warm-light family [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Pale Turtle Green in 740 of 23,781 paintings (3.11 percent), as photographed, almost always as a highlight [2]. It is heavily over-represented in work by Nicolas Lancret, over ten times the archive average, and in paintings from Tibet, 3.4 times the average [2]. It keeps company with Cream and Beige far more than chance [2]. These are screen approximations of aged, varnished canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
